title: CRLR/315/2024 of ARJUN SHARMA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.315 of 2024
Arjun Sharma .........Revisionist
Versus
State of Uttarakhand .........Respondent
Mr. Mayank Datta, Advocate for the revisionist through video
conferencing.
Mr. S.C. Dumka, learned AGA with Ms. Sweta B. Dobhal, learned Brief
Holder for the State.
Ms. Divya Jain, Advocate for the private respondent.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)
This revision preferred under Section 397 read
with Section 401 of the Cr.P.C. is directed against the order
dated 02.02.2024 and 01.03.2024 passed by learned 6th
Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun in Misc. Criminal Case
No.380 of 2023, Vadi vs. Vinod Singh Rana and others.
2. Facts in nutshell are that FIR No.140 of 2022, P.S.
Vasant Vihar, District Dehradun under the Gangsters Act was
instituted on the basis of four FIRs. The revisionist states
himself to be the victim and complainant in one of the FIR
i.e. FIR No.43 of 2017. In the said report, the final report
was submitted. The court concerned issued notice against the
said final report, in which, no objection was filed. The
revisionist then moved a protest petition before the court on
10.10.2023, but the court returned the protest petition to the
revisionist asking him to show his locus standi.
Subsequently, when the matter was transferred to another
court, the revisionist moved another application for the same
prayer. However, by order dated 02.02.2024 passed by
learned 6th Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun, the
1

application moved by the revisionist was rejected holding
that the revisionist has no locus standi in the matter.
Thereafter, another application dated 01.03.2024 was filed by
the revisionist, but the said application was also dismissed by
the court on the same date, i.e. 01.03.2024. Moreover, the
revisionist moved one another application before the DGP,
Uttarakhand requesting to take action against the erring
officer and to expunge the final report, therefore, requested
the Court by moving an application to defer the case till it is
decided by the DGP. The said application was also dismissed
by the court imposing the cost of Rs.1,000/- on the revisionist
by order dated 01.03.2024. Challenging those orders, present
revision has been filed.
3. In the instant matter, pursuant to FIR No.140 of
2022, a final report had been submitted by the police under
Section 173 Cr.P.C. In the Crime No.43 of 2017, the
advocates appearing for the informant as well as for the
accused had been given opportunity against the said final
report. It is the prerogative of the court either to accept the
final report submitted by the Investigating Officer or to take
other action as envisaged under Section 190 Cr.P.C. on the
said report. However, there is no ground to hear any other
party on the said report.
4. The instant case relates to Gangster Act even there
was no protest petition was filed. Hence, the court held that
the revisionist had no right of hearing. Accordingly, it
rejected the application by order dated 02.02.2024.
2

5. When another application was moved by the
informant on the ground of filing objection, the court held
that this application was nothing, but sheer abuse of process
of court in order to adjourn the proceeding of the case
unnecessarily. Accordingly, the adjournment application was
moved imposing a cost of Rs.1,000/-.
6. With the above observations, this Court is of the
view that there is no illegality or irregularity in the impugned
order. The revision fails and the same is dismissed at the
threshold.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.) 01.07.2025
Ravi
